title: Choose the visual world for UV GO
question: The roll assigned The Sundial. Keep it, take my pick or the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Sundial
options.lineage: garden and wall sundials: engraved hour lines, a gnomon's shadow, a motto plate
options.thesis: Today is a dial that only works in daylight; the shadow points to now and the best window is the lit sector.
materials: cast bronze reserved for your plan
options.viewport: Header and place line, then the answer card (window, verdict, reason) above a half-dial of today's daylight hours coloured by verdict, the free-time arc rimmed in bronze and a shadow hand at now; planner controls and checklist follow.
options.risk: A dial is less scannable than a strip at 13+ hours; it needs a linear fallback list and generous tap wedges to stay usable.

raised.raise: Strict colour budget: the shell is two stone inks; colour appears only as verdict or as the bronze plan mark.
One family throughout (Geist + Geist Mono numerals) on a 1px hairline grid; no shadowed cards.
A printed state vocabulary for hour marks: hairline at rest, filled selected, struck past, hollow dark, bracketed on focus.
Bronze is the course layer: used only for your free time and chosen window, never decoration.
The answer owns the first viewport; inputs collapse to one editable summary line above it.
Flat unmodulated fields only: no gradients, glass or glow anywhere.

options.label: Lifeguard Flags
options.lineage: beach lifeguard flag poles and chalked surf-condition boards
options.thesis: The verdict is a flag on a pole: everyone already knows green, yellow and red from the beach.
options.viewport: A tall flag-field verdict banner owns the top third with the window time on it, then the hour strip as a row of small pennants and the planner below.
options.risk: Familiar and literal; it is where most runs in this category land, and flag colour at page scale fights the timeline's own colour.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Hours as a strobing barcode field.
options.viewport: Barcode bars for each hour with dense numbers in the margin.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no colour breaks the required green/yellow/red verdict and everyday users cannot read it.
options.kept: Total palette commitment, kept as a strict colour budget.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Each window printed as a registered plate.
options.viewport: Result as a plate with crosshair corners and a mono token bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as a portfolio, not a daily outdoor check.
options.risk: Precious where it should be quick.
options.kept: One-family type discipline on a hairline grid.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: The day set as twin columns around a rail of hour keys.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns with an hour rail down the middle.
options.case: Fuses poorly: bookish density on a 390px phone, wrong audience.
options.kept: A printed state vocabulary for marks (rest, selected, past, dark, focus).

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Conditions as terrain, your plan as the purple course over it.
options.viewport: Hours as terrain bands with the free-time course drawn over them.
options.case: Fuses well on layering but users read it as a map of their location; loses both axes narrowly.
options.kept: One reserved ink for the user's plan, never decoration.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: Each window owns the screen; flick to the next.
options.viewport: Best window full screen, runner-ups one snap away.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hides the inputs and the timeline the brief requires.
options.risk: Navigation costume on a working tool.
options.kept: The answer owns the first viewport.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.thesis: Hours as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.viewport: A green lobe for the good window with capsule hour labels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: lobe colour competes with the verdict colours.
options.risk: Playful where calm and plain was asked.
options.kept: Flat unmodulated colour: no gradients, glass or glow.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean weather app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sky header with location and a large window time, white cards for verdict, hourly strip and checklist.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every weather app by design.
